note: Hebrew goren is the ordinary word for a threshing floor, an open flat area by the gate used for public assemblies; the KJV's "void place" guesses from the sense of open space.
The verb pittah means to entice or deceive (to lure someone into folly), which fits the lying spirit; "persuade" is too neutral.
Hebrew has the article, ha-ruach, "the spirit", which some take as a particular spirit (or the spirit of prophecy); the KJV makes it indefinite.

kjv: at a venture ... the joints of the harness
mine: at random ... between the joints of his armor and the breastplate
note: Hebrew le-tummo means "in his innocence", i.e. without aiming, and "harness" in 1611 meant body armour; the text names two pieces, ha-devaqim (the scale joints) and ha-shiryan (the breastplate).
Hebrew ve-ha-zonot rachatsu means "and the prostitutes washed"; the KJV follows a rabbinic interpretation that took zonot as "armour" (via zayin, "weapon"), which the grammar does not support.

Hebrew ha-qadesh denotes a male cult functionary/prostitute attached to a shrine (from qadosh, "consecrated"); "sodomites" names an ethnic origin and shifts the sense from cultic prostitution to sexual orientation.
